report.answer_text:
The explorer most often credited with leading an early voyage to Newfoundland's coast is John Cabot (Giovanni Caboto). He was an Italian navigator sailing for England under King Henry VII. He reached North America in 1497 and landed somewhere on the coast of present-day Newfoundland or nearby. Historians still debate the exact landfall. His reports of rich cod fishing grounds drew European fishermen to the region for centuries.
Some other early figures:
Leif Erikson (c. 1000 CE): The Norse reached the area around 1000 CE, about 500 years before Cabot. Archaeological remains at L'Anse aux Meadows in northern Newfoundland are the only confirmed Norse site in North America.
Gaspar Corte-Real (1500): This Portuguese explorer sailed to the region a few years after Cabot.
Jacques Cartier (1534): This French explorer passed through the Strait of Belle Isle and along Newfoundland's coast on his first voyage.
Sir Humphrey Gilbert (1583): He formally claimed Newfoundland for England at St. John's.
If your question comes from a particular class or quiz, the expected answer is most likely John Cabot.
